title: Tom Wallisch
body:
Tom Wallisch is a professional freeskier who came up through the same mid-Atlantic regional terrain-park scene as Dan Frank's adolescence — specifically showing up at Seven Springs and the neighboring Roundtop and Liberty resorts "a few times a year" during the 2000s, before the sport's media infrastructure caught up with him.

## The regional scene

The capture records Dan's adolescent experience of Wallisch directly: he would show up and "make a MESS of the park for a day" before deciding that Roundtop and Liberty — the less-developed parks — were preferable because of their scene culture. That scene culture, the "vibrant collection of people" at those smaller parks, became **4Bi9 Media**, the ski film company that would define the era's visual aesthetic and take the sport by storm.

Wallisch's documented competitive timeline — the "pretzel" grab (from the corpus's freeskiing research doc), the SuperUnknown video-contest breakout (same source), the 4Bi9 Media era (2007–2012) — maps onto the exact years after Dan's own adolescent skiing window. The capture itself names the pretzel and SuperUnknown as the era's defining markers; the [[wiki/people/tom-wallisch|Tom Wallisch]] page draws on both the operator capture and the pre-existing freeskiing raw doc for the competitive timeline. Dan's record is of encountering him as a local prodigy before he was famous, not as a peer.

## The Tanner Hall era context

The capture frames Dan's freeskiing adolescence as falling inside the "Tanner Hall era" — the moment when the skill threshold in slopestyle terrain-park skiing blew out. Johnny Mosely's earlier-generation tricks gave way to Candide Thovex corking 450s onto flat-down rails with style. Wallisch is the era-defining athlete at the top of that expansion: a regional mid-Atlantic skier who turned the infrastructure that existed at places like Seven Springs into a professional platform.

## Corpus context

Dan's documented relationship to Wallisch is an adult retrospective research interest, not a personal friendship. The [[wiki/places/seven-springs|Seven Springs]] page names the shared home turf as the specific cultural backdrop that gives Dan's ski years a precise geographic anchor. The capture distinguishes between knowing of Wallisch as a local prodigy and having any personal connection to him.

## Gaps

No direct contact between Dan and Tom Wallisch is documented. The nature and extent of Wallisch's attendance at Seven Springs and Roundtop during Dan's adolescence comes from a single retrospective capture and is not independently confirmed from video archives or other sources.
